messages:
rachel: Heads-up - release pipeline tripped on sample-sdk publish. Changelog generator pulled in typegen diffs and created a minor bump.
rachel: release log: https://release.company/flow/9001
ci-bot: publish job failed: change detected in generated types -> manual approval required
anya: Is this a real API change or just generated ordering/whitespace diffs?
sam: Looks generated. I ran `git show --name-only HEAD` and only `sample-sdk/dist/index.d.ts` changed after regen. No openapi or handwritten code touched.
lina: The changelog script currently treats any diff as a user-facing change. It can't distinguish generated-only edits. We should teach it to ignore patterns like `dist/**/*.d.ts` and `types/generated/**`.
rachel: Also, the automated semver bump picked `minor` because a public interface changed according to the script. We don't want noise releases for regenerated artifacts.
sam: Short-term mitigation: add a release-gate that checks `git diff --name-only` and if only matched ignored globs, skip auto-bump and mark for human review. devex-bot can add a label `regen-only`.
devex-bot: Suggestion: new CI step `release:regen-check` that runs in the draft release job and posts a regen-diff comment with reproduction steps.
anya: We should also ensure typegen diffs can't accidentally tighten types that break consumers. Add a small integration test to the sample-sdk repo that compiles a minimal consumer against the published types. If consumer compile fails, block release.
lina: I can add `consumer-compile` GH action that `npm pack` the current build and `tsc --project` a sample consumer directory. Will post a PR.
rachel: Good. For this immediate run: I'll revert the auto-bump and mark the release as `on-hold` until we confirm it's generated-only.
release-bot: release marked on-hold. Filed REL-907.
ci-bot: created comment with diff and command to reproduce: `yarn regen && git --no-pager diff -- sample-sdk/dist`
sam: Also want to improve the changelog heuristics: if only exported types changed (dts diffs) and runtime JS is identical, treat as patch or skip. We can check checksum of built JS vs previous.
anya: Great idea. That helps catch cases where types drift but runtime is stable. But we need process for intentional API changes (we should still ship a minor/major when runtime changes).
lina: I'll add both checks: (1) `release:regen-check` to detect regen-only diffs, (2) `release:runtime-check` that compares `lib/*.js` checksums vs last release.
rachel: Can we also surface the diff in PRs when `dev-toolchain.lock` changes? Prevent surprises from transitive bumps.
devex-bot: I'll post a reply-to-PR action: when `dev-toolchain.lock` or `package-lock.json` changes and includes `typegen` version bump, post regen-diff and require `@devex` review.
sam: Until the automation lands, policy: any PR that bumps typegen requires an explicit `devex-approve` label and a regen-diff artifact included.
rachel: Sounds good. I'll open the revert PR to un-bump the toolchain for this release and follow up with the devex PRs to land the checks.
anya: Thanks — let's avoid shipping a semver change for generated-only edits. Ping here when revert lands. :thumbsup:
